title: Bound rounded block-solve error at the fine-prime Gaussian boundary
body:
I instantiate the retained block-factor rounding handoff at PR4100's narrow Gaussian boundary gap `delta>=1/(16p²)`. I keep the original two-product block order and exact dyadic Strassen products, then round coefficient/inverse pages and completed RHS/solution blocks. I derive the complete residual before bounding the rounded state, so the error estimate has no factor equal to the number of row blocks.

For `eta=2^(1-P)` and `Y0=max(1,||RHS||max)`, the condition `eta<=2^-21*p^-9` gives two-pass solution error below `2^40*p^16*eta*Y0`, output magnitude at most `2^20*p^7*Y0`, and exact arithmetic temporaries at most `2^46*p^16*Y0` on the `2P` grid. These explicit constants give O(p)-bit words when P and log(Y0) are O(p). I account for rounded diagonal-block inverses, consecutive-block geometry, both upper-pass reversals and temporary padding. I preserve the complete ceiling-based batching tariff and its `R>=w` simplification boundary.

I execute the authenticated retained `block_solve` and recursive `mul` through a rounding adapter. Independent ordinary elimination and matrix products supply exact solutions and residuals. Fifteen systems cover sixty triangular passes, 548 matrix products and 12,164 actual Strassen leaf products. All fifteen have nonzero rounding error. Controls distinguish an inverse of a rounded block from a rounded reference inverse, nonconsecutive inverse blocks, insufficient precision, wrong direction, unhandled corners, omitted predecessor blocks and omitted output rounding.

At head `a20501df8fc07f5ceb32e6fd64bce9ad8fe594bf`, both registered ordinary/optimized checks pass. I passed the 20-file committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export integrity. Both Git-free export commands pass in 0.422 and 0.430 seconds, with all 21 files including the receipt unchanged. Export SHA256: `4c422a21fc5860d92818d4ed5a6b4f6c2072296c8a39466ec63cfac768993dd5`; receipt SHA256: `2901b6f41cbe4f40814737949ffd95a280d6a8fa9d8aa7da6d4fda1ea2a0fc63`. Scientific receipt: `4941625250a4d71c7c76ba4963e1593b5fddf48cffd3b0bc121e1de4cf82ebfb`.

I matched both successful [hosted records](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39417123250) to the committed export and checked the successful unchanged-input step. Test merge `11b0d728a4a4d8f0f60bb89fb50489617c0719b5` has the published tree `281da10ce2985fc3e81283dbe3167a03d63a20d0`.

I start from canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7, and pin PR4100 at `337d04939571a637aeab54a0f58f54fde811663a`. I refreshed main, source feedback and 100 recent PR records before publication. [Discussion4182](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4182) records the claim, bounded overlap, complete obligation ledger and prior coverage. The new PR4184 free-word audit is complementary.

I restrict the theorem to the stated naturally ordered finite-section narrow boundary and exact reference LU/inverse-page preparation. I do not assert the same result for an arbitrary rounded LU factorization, unhandled cyclic geometry or a broad Schur inverse. Physical factor-page/tape integration, analytic reference preparation and complete multiplication-theorem acceptance remain separate. I keep the selected frontier unchanged.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. I credit Vlado Vojdanovski's block proposal and prototype, the earlier qualitative stability and Schur audits, Cinna Davis's conditioning argument, the original Gaussian/Harvey–van der Hoeven lineage, and the scalar physical solver's prior residual analysis. I retain the classical Strassen and stability attribution. Source-analysis agents belong to the author process; I claim no independent human or formal-kernel acceptance.
